title: Daily 07:00 IST digest + weekly Sunday 18:00 IST list-ready email (Resend) + in-app badges
goal: Ship F14/REQ-20's notifications: a daily digest that fires only when something is due within 3 days, a weekly 'next week's list ready' digest, both sent by email via Resend, plus in-app badges showing the same due-soon count where the app already links to /plan. Reuse S-22's getDueSoonItems() (lib/plan/data.ts) as the single source of truth for 'due soon' rather than re-deriving a second definition -- it already excludes snoozed/skipped-active/excluded plan states and already documents itself as 'F14's digest threshold.'
in_scope: **Migration (additive): households gets one new nullable column, notify_email text.** No write path is built for it in this story -- same precedent as households.monthly_budget (E-0, still unset for every real household, no UI until S-33/E-14 Settings). Confirmed via grep before writing this spec: no email/notify column exists on households today. Both real households have notify_email=null after this migration; the digest and weekly routes must treat null as an honest, silent skip (see below), not an error.

**Resend integration: plain fetch to https://api.resend.com/emails, no npm dependency added.** RESEND_API_KEY is present as an env slot in .env.local/.env.example but is BLANK -- confirmed before writing this spec, same shape as CRON_SECRET's own 'not verified live from this session' note. Do not install the `resend` SDK package (its surface can't be exercised without a real key in this environment; a plain fetch call is a smaller, equally-real integration). The send function must return a structured result -- never a bare boolean, never a 200 that reads as delivered when it wasn't: `{ sent: boolean, reason?: string }`. Skip (sent:false) honestly, with a specific reason string, whenever RESEND_API_KEY is unset OR household.notify_email is null OR the due-item list is empty -- never fabricate a 'sent' result.

**`lib/notifications/digest.ts` (server-only): `buildDailyDigest()` and `buildWeeklyDigest()`, both thin wrappers that call `getDueSoonItems(3)` / `getDueSoonItems(7)` (imported, not re-derived) and format the result into a subject + plain-text body.** Daily subject/framing: '<N> item(s) due soon' (per REQ-20's literal 'daily digest if anything is due within 3 days'). Weekly subject/framing: 'Next week's shopping list is ready' (per F14's literal wording), using the 7-day window as the working definition of 'next week' -- no separate shopping-list-generation call, this reuses the same due-soon data at a wider window rather than inventing a second 'what's coming up' computation.

**`POST /api/cron/digest-daily`**: same CRON_SECRET fail-closed auth pattern as the existing `/api/cron/recompute-stats` route (unset secret is never treated as 'no auth required'). Calls buildDailyDigest(); if dueCount===0, returns `{ sent: false, reason: 'nothing due within 3 days', dueCount: 0 }` without attempting a send at all (this IS the epic's acceptance criterion: digest only fires when something is actually due). If dueCount>0, attempts the Resend send and returns the structured send result plus dueCount.

**`POST /api/cron/digest-weekly`**: same auth pattern. Calls buildWeeklyDigest(); same empty-list skip logic (not a hard acceptance criterion for the weekly send per backlog/PRD wording, but the same honest-skip behavior applies for consistency -- no product reason to email an empty 'next week' list).

**vercel.json: two new cron entries.** Daily 07:00 IST = 01:30 UTC -> `"30 1 * * *"`. Weekly Sunday 18:00 IST = 12:30 UTC Sunday -> `"30 12 * * 0"`. Verified before writing this spec: Vercel Hobby plan (this project's confirmed plan, from the linked VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN) allows up to 100 cron jobs per project, each capped at a max frequency of once per day -- both new entries plus the existing nightly recompute-stats entry are well within that (three daily-or-less jobs total). Hobby-plan timing is only guaranteed within the specified hour, not to the exact minute -- documented as a residual risk, not a defect.

**In-app badges: extend the existing due-count idiom (already shipped on /plan's cadence-bucket tabs, e.g. 'Weekly (3)') to the Today page's outbound links.** app/page.tsx already computes `dueSoon` (S-22's getDueSoonItems, same list the digest reuses) and already renders it in full as a 'Due soon' card -- add a matching `(N)` badge to the existing 'View plan' link using that same already-computed count, no new query. This repo has no global nav (noted in every prior epic); Today is the one surface every session lands on after onboarding, so it's the correct (and only sane) home for this badge given the constraint.
out_of_scope: Any Settings UI to set households.notify_email -- belongs to S-33/E-14, same precedent as monthly_budget's own no-write-path gap. Without a set notify_email, both digest routes run for real (auth, due-count computation, in-app badge logic all fully live-verifiable) but every send attempt honestly skips with reason 'no notify_email configured' -- this is expected and reported as a residual risk in the ledger, not a blocker for the rest of the story.

Actually sending a real email end-to-end with a live Resend account -- RESEND_API_KEY is genuinely unconfigured in this environment (confirmed, not assumed) and creating a third-party account/API key is outside this session's authority. The send code path is real (plain fetch, correct headers/body per Resend's documented API shape) and will function the moment a key is added; it is not exercised live in this story's verification, and that gap is reported explicitly rather than glossed over.
Web push / VAPID / any push-notification provider -- working spec F14 states explicitly 'No web push in v1.' Confirmed before any design work began; not part of this story's scope in any form.

A global nav bar or a persistent badge icon -- no such surface exists anywhere in this app yet (established constraint, every prior UI-adding epic has hit and noted it); the Today-page link badge is the in-scope, consistent-with-precedent choice.
Any change to getDueSoonItems()'s own logic or its 3-day default -- reused verbatim as the shared 'due soon' source of truth for both the digest and the badge, not re-implemented.
acceptance: Digest only fires when something is actually due within 3 days.
invariants: The daily digest route never calls Resend when the due-soon list (3-day window) is empty -- the literal acceptance criterion. Verified at the gate's boundaries: due in 3 days in, due in 4 days out, due today in, overdue in; snoozed/skipped-active/excluded items excluded even if their underlying due date would otherwise qualify (getDueSoonItems already guarantees this, re-verified live for this story rather than assumed).
Both cron routes fail closed on missing/incorrect CRON_SECRET, same as the existing recompute-stats route -- an unset secret is never treated as 'no auth required.'

A send attempt is never reported as sent:true unless Resend's API actually returned success -- RESEND_API_KEY unset, notify_email unset, and empty due-list are all distinct, honestly-labeled skip reasons, never silently coalesced into a fake success.

notify_email is PII once a real value exists -- migration is additive/nullable only, no value is fabricated or backfilled, and this is called out explicitly in the PR body's security-gate section even though no write path exists yet in this story.
